page: Amazon Web Services m8azn.xlarge is a general-purpose cloud instance built on the Nitro hypervisor and driven by the x86_64 AMD EPYC 9R05 processor. The instance provides 4 dedicated physical cores without simultaneous multithreading, running at a clock frequency of 5.0 GHz. The processor features 48 KB L1d cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 20 MB L3 cache, with hardware support for AVX-512 extensions including VNNI and BF16, alongside cryptographic acceleration instructions like AES, VAES, and SHA-NI. It includes 16.0 GB of DDR5 system memory clocked at 6 GHz, establishing a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio. Networking performance provides an 8 Gbps baseline. There is no bundled local storage or integrated GPU hardware, meaning all non-volatile storage relies on network-attached EBS volumes.

Benchmark results highlight exceptionally strong single-core CPU throughput, driven by the 5.0 GHz clock speed. In synthetic testing, the instance achieved top-tier rankings in stress-ng single-core performance (4213.99) and Geekbench single-core score (3118.0), alongside top-decile throughput in single-threaded gzip compression (46.2 GB/sec) and bzip3 decompression (20.52 GB/sec). Text generation speed for a small 135M parameter language model also scored in the top tier at 452.13 tokens per second. In contrast, multi-threaded metrics scale across the 4 physical cores into the mid-tier spectrum, including a multi-core stress-ng rating of 16812.35, a Geekbench multi-core score of 9949.0, and a PassMark CPU score of 15118.97.

Memory and network operations exhibit balanced baseline metrics suited for general workloads. The DDR5 subsystem achieved 103.7 GB/sec for uncached read operations and 68.41 GB/sec for large block writes. In application-focused benchmarks, the instance registered 16.87 million operations per second for Redis SET workloads and 26.64 GB/sec in static web serving throughput. From an architectural efficiency perspective, the provision of fully dedicated physical cores ensures predictable execution, though overall multithreaded capacity is naturally bounded by the modest 4-core footprint.

The Amazon Web Services m8azn.xlarge instance is effective for single-thread sensitive applications, microservices, continuous integration pipelines, moderate-scale web serving, and lightweight caching tiers that benefit from high clock speeds and DDR5 memory without requiring local disk storage or GPU acceleration.
description: Amazon Web Services m8azn.xlarge is a general-purpose, Nitro-based instance powered by a 4-core AMD EPYC 9R05 processor operating at 5.0 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. Featuring 4 dedicated physical cores with single-thread allocation, it is paired with 16.0 GB of DDR5 memory at 6 GHz and an 8 Gbps baseline network interface. The instance does not bundle local disk storage or hardware GPUs. In benchmark evaluations, m8azn.xlarge demonstrates top-tier single-threaded performance, recording a Geekbench single-core score of 3118.0 and 46.2 GB/sec in single-thread gzip compression, while multi-core metrics reflect the 4-core configuration with an average Geekbench multi-core score of 9949.0. Operating with a 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM balance, it provides steady performance for compute tasks sensitive to clock speeds, small-scale web serving, and application hosting.
